newsitem.title: USA: Exactech hip system wins FDA approval.
newsitem.headline: Exactech hip system wins FDA approval.

text.p: Exactech Inc said on Thursday that it received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval to market its AuRA cemented total hip system.

AuRA is a system of forged femoral components used for primary or first-time hip replacements, earlier replacements, fractures and bone tumor surgical procedures. The company said the market for the hip system was worth about $73 million.
Exactech said the AuRA system reduced operating room time and processing costs.

Exactech President and Chief Operating Officer Timothy Seese said: "AuRA will substantially increase Exactech's participation in the fracture market and will enable our company to enter the $73 million revision hip market, a segment that comprises 10.8 percent of the total hip market and is growing faster than the overall hip market."
Exactech reported 1995 sales of $4.89 million for its hip replacement system. Seese said he expected AuRA to boost the company's revenues in the hip market segment.
The product was scheduled to be released generally in the first quarter 1997, the company said.
